messages:
maria_support: FYI customer AcmeHealth opened an escalation — they say p99 latency jumped yesterday after we pushed 2.1.3. They see streaming responses TTFB fine but total time (TTLB) is much higher, lots of tiny chunks. repro + logs attached in their ticket.

sophia_cs: +1 got the ticket, forwarded the customer profile. They're on Dedicated in eu-west-1 with reserved capacity. Said it started at ~10:40 UTC yesterday.

maria_support: pasted customer example request (they're using our streaming endpoint):

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-7b-stream-quant","prompt":"summarize...","stream":true}'
```

maria_support: Customer notes: TTFB ~120ms, then 40-60 tiny chunks over 3s, but server reported compute done at ~1.1s. So client sees 3.1s TTLB.

aj_sre: Interesting — smells like flush cadence / proxy buffering between runtime and edge. Could be our nginx/gateway or edge CDN coalescing small writes. @devon_runtime can you check runtime flush behavior in 2.1.3? We changed the small-chunk coalescing heuristic there.

devon_runtime: I pulled the rollout diffs. 2.1.3 introduced a change: adaptive_flush_window default lowered from 80ms -> 20ms for streaming to reduce latency on low-latency infra. That reduced TTFB for some flows but increased network packet rate for others, leading to downstream buffering thrash. I think that's the culprit.

liam_product: We tuned that to optimize average latency; didn't fully simulate multi-hop buffering. Customer load + Dedicated network might push them into a bad spot.

aj_sre: Repro steps I ran against eu-west canary: send the same streaming request, capture TCP segments (tcpdump) and our runtime logs. I see many small write() syscalls followed by the gateway ACKs but edge (fastly/nginx) buffers until ~1KB and then flushes, causing perceived delay.

aj_sre: snippet from tcpdump + timing (simplified):

```
0.120s server: first chunk (20 bytes)
0.140s server: chunk (18 bytes)
0.160s server: chunk (22 bytes)
... compute complete @1.10s
1.10s server: final chunk (700 bytes)
1.12s edge: flush to client -> large burst seen by client @3.10s
```

devon_runtime: That matches the adaptive_flush_window change. Small chunk train + downstream coalescing -> client sees high TTLB. For non-streaming clients they get the combined output fast.

maria_support: Customer asks for short-term mitigation now. Any quick fixes we can apply on their account/route? They can't accept 3s TTLB.

devon_runtime: Short-term options:
- bump adaptive_flush_window back to 80ms on their runtime instance (config toggle per-tenant). This will group small writes into fewer flushes.
- or provide a non-streaming fallback route for them (we can set stream=false on their route and serve the same model sync). That will remove streaming overhead entirely.
- or add a header to the gateway to disable downstream buffering (depends on CDN). Might be hit-or-miss with customer network.

aj_sre: I recommend 1) toggle their adaptive_flush_window to 80ms and 2) enable a route-level flag to prefer sync for that customer until we have a permanent fix. Both are low risk.

sophia_cs: Customer prefers minimal changes — they're okay with a temporary route change to non-streaming if perf improves. They want us to measure before/after and keep them in loop.

maria_support: I'll ask for permission and schedule change. Do we need an eng review before toggling adaptive_flush_window on Dedicated? @devon_runtime

devon_runtime: It's safe to change per-tenant. It will slightly increase server-side tail latency in some small cases, but for this customer the net TTLB will drop. I'll prepare the config change and a one-click rollback.

deploy-bot: Deployment requested: patch/runtime-config@prod -> change adaptive_flush_window=80ms for tenant acmehealth. Approving deploy window: immediate. CI: green.

deploy-bot: Deployment completed at 1951234589. canary health: ok.

repro-bot: Repro test run: 10 requests, streaming endpoint vs sync fallback. Results (median / p99):
- streaming (pre-change): median 220ms / p99 3.1s
- streaming (post-change): median 240ms / p99 1.25s
- sync fallback: median 1.05s / p99 1.2s

aj_sre: Good. TTLB/p99 for streaming improved significantly after bump. Sync fallback also acceptable; but streaming post-change gives best tradeoff.

maria_support: Shared results with customer and asked them to confirm whether to keep the adaptive_flush_window or stay on sync fallback. Waiting on reply.

liam_product: Action items for product/eng: reevaluate default adaptive_flush_window tuning (maybe region-aware) and add a test harness that simulates multi-hop buffering (gateway + CDN) in CI.

devon_runtime: Agreed. I'll open a PR to add a multi-hop simulation test and propose a config change that is region/stack-aware. Also will add a per-tenant rollout toggle to make rollbacks trivial.

sophia_cs: Customer confirmed they see improved perf and prefer to stay with streaming + adjusted flush window. Thanks team :tada:

maria_support: Closing loop with customer. I'll mark escalation resolved and note rollback path if regression reappears. Filing postmortem doc in #incidents.

maria_support: TL;DR: 2.1.3 reduced flush window (20ms) -> increased small-chunk traffic -> downstream buffering => TTLB p99 spike for some Dedicated customers. Mitigated by bumping adaptive_flush_window to 80ms for affected tenant and offering sync fallback. Followups: test harness + region-aware defaults.
